question.text: At $80^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the vapour pressure of pure liquid ' $A$ ' is $520 \mathrm{~mm} \mathrm{Hg}$ and that of pure liquid ' $B$ ' is $1000 \mathrm{~mm}$ $\mathrm{Hg}$. If a mixture solution of ' $A$ ' and ' $B$ ' boils at $80^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $1 \mathrm{~atm}$ pressure, the amount of ' $A$ ' in the mixture is $(1 \mathrm{~atm}=760 \mathrm{~mm} \mathrm{Hg})$

solution.text:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& P_T=P_A^{\circ} X_A+P_B^{\circ} X_B \\
& 760=520 X_A+P_B^{\circ}\left(1-X_A\right) \\
& \Rightarrow X_A=0.5
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus, mole $\%$ of $A=50 \%$
